name: Northern Ireland
note: In Northern Ireland the doctor who treated the deceased within 28 days for a natural illness gives the medical certificate of cause of death directly to the registrar, by approved electronic means since March 2026; there is no medical examiner, and unnatural, unexplained or untreated deaths go to the coroner, who must also be told by police of bodies found and suspicious deaths. A relative (or other qualified informant) must give the particulars to any registrar within five days, in person, by telephone or electronically, and the registrar issues the certificate for burial or cremation. Registrars must send death particulars to the Department for Communities, but Tell Us Once does not operate for Northern Ireland residents, so the family tells passport, driving-licence, tax and other bodies one by one. The Registrar General has a discretionary power to notify persons the informant names.

steps.title: Death is verified by a doctor, nurse or paramedic
steps.who: In practice the family doctor (or on-call doctor) for an expected death at home, ambulance staff for an unexpected one, and hospital or care-home staff where the death occurs there; no statute names who may verify.
steps.summary: The Births and Deaths Registration (NI) Order 1976, the Coroners Act (NI) 1959 and the Deaths, Still-Births and Baby Loss Act (NI) 2026 were read and say nothing about verifying the fact of death. Official guidance (nidirect) tells families to call the family doctor for an expected death and 999 for an unexpected one, when ambulance staff confirm the death.

steps.title: Doctor (and others) must report unnatural or untreated deaths to the coroner
steps.who: Every medical practitioner, registrar of deaths, funeral undertaker, occupier of the house, and person in charge of an institution where the deceased lived.
steps.trigger: Reason to believe the death resulted from violence, misadventure, unfair means, negligence or malpractice, or from any cause other than a natural illness for which the deceased was seen and treated by a doctor within 28 days.
steps.summary: Where a death is referred to the coroner, the doctor must not give the registrar a medical certificate and the five-day registration duty is displaced.

steps.title: Police notify the coroner of bodies found and unexplained deaths
steps.who: The police officer for the district where the body is found or the death occurs.
steps.trigger: A dead body is found, or an unexpected, unexplained or suspicious death occurs.
steps.summary: Written notice with whatever information the police can obtain.

steps.title: Treating doctor gives the medical certificate of cause of death to the registrar electronically
steps.who: The registered medical practitioner who treated the deceased for the natural illness within 28 days before death.
steps.trigger: A death from natural illness not referred to the coroner.
steps.summary: Since 23 March 2026 the certificate must be given by approved electronic means; in practice it goes to the General Register Office for Northern Ireland, which routes it to the registration office for the deceased's home address. There is no medical examiner scrutiny.

steps.title: Informant gives the particulars to any registrar
steps.who: In order: any relative with knowledge of the particulars; then anyone present at the death; then the executor or administrator, the occupier, the person finding or taking charge of the body, or the person procuring disposal.

deadline.text: within five days from the date of death (fourteen days if the registrar has been notified and holds the medical certificate)

steps.summary: Since 23 March 2026 the informant may attend any register office, or give the particulars by telephone or approved electronic means; the registrar usually telephones the informant. Failure by a first-instance informant is an offence.

steps.title: Registrar issues the certificate for burial or cremation
steps.who: The registrar, to the informant (on request) and to the person who effects the disposal or performs the funeral service.
steps.trigger: Registration, or notice of the death with the medical certificate already received; not where the coroner has authorised burial or cremation.
steps.summary: The certificate is issued free and lets the funeral director proceed.

steps.title: Anyone may obtain a certified copy (full or short) of the death entry
steps.who: Any person, from the registrar at registration or from the General Register Office for Northern Ireland afterwards.
steps.summary: Any person may search the indexes and require a certified copy; a short certificate without the cause of death is available for deaths registered after 17 December 2012.

steps.title: Registrar sends death particulars to the Department for Communities
steps.who: Each registrar of births and deaths, for deaths they register (originally to the Department of Health and Social Services; social security functions now sit with the Department for Communities).

deadline.text: as soon as it is reasonably practicable

steps.latencyNote: as soon as it is reasonably practicable to do so (ssndni-1987-r3)
steps.summary: Name, date of death, sex, maiden surname, date of birth and usual address are furnished in writing or on data material.

steps.title: Family reports the death to the Department for Communities Bereavement Service
steps.who: A relative or other person dealing with the deceased's affairs.
steps.trigger: The death of someone receiving social security benefits, State Pension or Pension Credit.
steps.summary: The Bereavement Service records the date of death and tells each office that paid benefit, and takes claims for bereavement payments. It covers Department for Communities benefits only; Tell Us Once is not available for Northern Ireland residents.

steps.title: Family returns and cancels the passport
steps.summary: HM Passport Office (or the Irish passport office for Irish passports) is told separately.

steps.title: Family tells the Driver Vehicle Agency
steps.summary: Driving licences, vehicle tax and registration documents are dealt with by the Northern Ireland Driver Vehicle Agency, contacted directly.

steps.title: Family tells the tax office and other government bodies
steps.summary: The tax office, National Insurance Contributions Office, Child Benefit Office, Land and Property Services (rates) and the council are each told separately.

steps.title: Registrar General may notify persons of the registered death
steps.who: The Registrar General, on its own initiative or on an application (with fee) by the person who gave the information for registration.
steps.trigger: Registration and, usually, the informant's application.
steps.summary: A discretionary power to notify persons the Registrar General considers appropriate, subject to conditions; it is not a general verification service.

steps.title: Family tells banks, insurers and pension providers
steps.summary: Banks, building societies, insurers, pension providers and other private bodies rely on the family, usually with a death certificate.

steps.title: Personal representatives may advertise for creditors in the Belfast Gazette

deadline.text: claims period of not less than two months

steps.summary: Advertisement once in the Belfast Gazette and twice in two daily newspapers protects the personal representatives against unknown claims.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Five days from the date of death; fourteen days where the registrar has been notified and holds the medical certificate; suspended where the coroner is involved.

informantDuty.note: Relatives with knowledge first, then persons present, then executor, occupier, finder or the person procuring disposal.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No medical examiner system: the treating doctor gives the certificate straight to the registrar.

electronicRegistration.note: Since 23 March 2026 the medical certificate must be given by approved electronic means and the informant may give the particulars by telephone or approved electronic means instead of attending.

certificateAccess.note: Any person may obtain a certified copy; a short certificate omitting the cause of death is also available.

governmentPropagation.note: Registrars must notify the Department for Communities, but Tell Us Once is not available; passport, driving licence (DVA), tax and rates bodies are told by the family one by one.

privateSectorVerification.note: No death-data service for private bodies; the Registrar General has only a discretionary power to notify persons of a registered death, usually on the informant's application.

gaps: The Social Security (Notification of Deaths) Regulations (NI) 1987 are available on legislation.gov.uk only as the original PDF (text verified from it); whether they have been amended or replaced, and whether the duty now runs to the Department for Communities by transfer of functions, was not confirmed.
The Registration of Births and Deaths Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2012 (amended by the 2026 Act, s. 7) were not read directly; the telephone/electronic routes are cited from the amending section.
No source was found for how the Chief Electoral Officer for Northern Ireland learns of deaths (Representation of the People (NI) Regulations 2008 not searched in full).
nidirect pages on the coroner (/articles/coroners-post-mortems-and-inquests) were not read; coroner duties are cited from the Coroners Act (NI) 1959.
Whether the Registrar General actually operates an art. 40B notification service for informants (forms, fees) was not confirmed.

No Department of Health (NI) guidance on verification of death was found: the health-ni.gov.uk site search returns its whole index whatever the query, and guessed publication paths 404. The verify step rests on statutory silence and nidirect.
